items.followUp: Define a cation and explain how it is formed.

rubric.why: An anion is identified by its negative charge.
rubric.description: Defines an anion as a negatively charged ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a negative ion.

rubric.why: An anion forms when an atom or group gains electrons.
rubric.description: Explains that an anion is formed by gaining one or more electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons are gained.

modelAnswer: An anion is a negatively charged ion.
It is formed when an atom or group of atoms gains one or more electrons.

items.followUp: Why does atomic radius generally increase down a group?

rubric.why: Additional electron shells place the outer electrons farther from the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that the number of shells increases or that the outer electrons are farther from the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either the increased-shells reason or the increased-distance reason.

rubric.why: Increased shielding reduces nuclear attraction, so less energy is needed to remove an outer electron.
rubric.description: Explains that increased shielding reduces attraction to the outer electrons and lowers the energy needed to remove one.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking shielding or reduced nuclear attraction to the decrease in ionization energy.

modelAnswer: Down a group, the number of electron shells increases, so the outer electrons are farther from the nucleus.
Shielding also increases, reducing the nuclear attraction on the outer electrons; therefore, less energy is needed to remove an electron.

items.followUp: What is a double covalent bond? Explain with an example.

rubric.why: A single covalent bond consists of one pair of electrons shared between two atoms.
rubric.description: Defines a single covalent bond as one shared pair of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two atoms share one pair of electrons.

rubric.why: A valid example identifies a molecule in which atoms share one pair of electrons.
rubric.description: Gives an appropriate example, such as H₂ or Cl₂, and identifies the shared pair.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example with the sharing of one pair stated.

modelAnswer: A single covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one pair of electrons.
For example, in H₂, each hydrogen atom contributes one electron and the two atoms share the pair, forming an H–H single covalent bond.
